title: The Lesson learned! Check your data.
author: mrfunkm
selftext:
Can’t believe 3 weeks building this bot, tuning the entry and exit. Working with different analysis etc also wondered why my RSI detection never felt good ..  although I’m getting a 70% win rate. Never hitting any decent entry points

.. turns out the free Alpaca Rest API is 15min delayed ffs 🤦.. just flipped to its Iive websocket feed which, …. Luckily still paper trading.

Can’t believe I missed this.  

Hopefully will get some better performance..  what would I expect to see?

comments.author: jp-fanguin
comments.body:
I get mine from databento and massive.com for backtest. 

For real live feed, I have a propfirm that give me a Rithmic live feed. 

The broker, I believe, is supposed to give you this live feed.

comments.author: DarkandBoring
comments.body: But if your getting your prices from the same place that the engine is trading on?  Confused on why that would make a difference?

comments.author: DarkandBoring
comments.body: So your pulling prices from one place then placing orders on another api?

comments.author: Tall_Brick_1310
comments.body: I faced a similar challenge initially when I was getting data with Yahoo finance and looking at the charts on TradingView. I then switched to using oanda data with their API and then getting the same on TradingView with oanda as the provider

replies.author: mrfunkm
replies.body: Thanks.. so I switched fully over to alpaca websocket now, not only was I using delayed Alpaca Rest api for my entries, for my open positions and exit I was using yfinance which I understand has its own unique delay, so double whammy. Quite excited for tomorrow 😉

comments.author: LectureElectronic207
comments.body: yeah that delay can fully distort results. expect your performance to change once you switch to live data
